page: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is an x86_64 server belonging to the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, with 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 11519 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3079.05 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2084.0, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Text processing is a notable strength, achieving a top-tier Geekbench text processing score of 2766.0. Multi-core and memory operations generally perform in the average range, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 12359.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 26168.72. However, a key performance bottleneck is the uncached read-only memory bandwidth for large blocks, which measured at a weak 36.77 GB/sec. Large-model LLM prompt processing is also a limitation, with the 70B model processing at a poor 4.44 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L16aos_v4 offers a high density of local storage of over 11 TB paired with a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1 to 8, making it a resource-dense option for workloads requiring significant local data caching without the overhead of external storage attachments. The combination of high local storage capacity, strong single-core execution, and average database operation performance makes this server suitable for relational databases, local data warehousing, text processing pipelines, and medium-scale web serving.
